text:
B: Hi. Gareth. Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah, hiya. Dean.
B: Hi Dean. Where are you?
A: Tipton. West Midlands.
B: Maidstone, Kent. I'll be honest, I noticed the shirt on your photo.
A: [laughs] Ar, everybody does. West Brom.
B: I'm Charlton. So I can't really talk.
A: Charlton. Ar. You've had it rough.
B: It's always the hope that kills you, mate.
A: Yeah. We've got none of that left.
B: That's what the Walsall lad said. What do you do?
A: Press operator. Metal pressings, Wednesbury. You?
B: Civil engineer. Drainage, flood risk. Bit of office, bit of site.
A: Ar, I seen the hi-vis on the door. Thought you might be on site.
B: Sometimes, yeah. Mostly standing in a field looking at a ditch, if I'm honest.
A: [laughs] Sounds alright.
B: It has its moments. Do you like the press work?
A: Yeah, it's steady. You get a jam, the gaffer shouts, you sort it, you carry on. I don't get rattled, really.
B: Same sort of thing with me. People panic, I just sort of stand there and think.
A: Ar. Somebody's got to.
B: What do you do outside work?
A: Outside work, er... fishing. Canal, or the pool near Himley. And the PlayStation, late.
B: Fishing, I've never really done it. My dad used to, on the Medway. I might take him, actually. He's had a stroke, couple of years ago, so he can't do the walking he used to, but sitting on a bank he could probably manage.
A: Ar, it's good for that. Me dad had a heart scare couple of years back.
B: Oh, right. Is he alright now?
A: Yeah, he's alright. Tablets and that. Mum watches what he eats. It was a bit, er... you know. You don't know what to say, really.
B: No. I was the same. I did all the forms, the care plan, the hospital stuff. Never really talked about it, though. Not to anyone.
A: Ar. Same. I just sort of went round more.
B: That probably counts, to be fair.
A: Yeah. Maybe.
B: Have you got kids?
A: Ruby. Eight. Kayleigh's daughter, but, you know.
B: Yeah. Mine's nine, Alfie. I help coach his under-tens on Saturdays.
A: Are they any good?
B: They lost seven-one last week. Nobody minded. They were more bothered about the orange slices.
A: [laughs] Ruby'd be the same. She'd be picking daisies.
B: There's always one doing that. Usually in goal.
A: [laughs] Ar.
B: Do you take her fishing?
A: Once. She got bored after ten minutes, wanted to go to the park.
B: Ten minutes is good going, honestly. Alfie wouldn't last—
